title: Post-Quantum Encryption: Why Prepare Before Quantum Computers?
headline:
Why prepare for
a computer not here yet?
meaning: Some public-key systems face a future quantum threat.
example: Recorded encrypted data may stay sensitive for years.
comparison: Post-quantum cryptography runs on ordinary computers.
caution: It is about migration, not an instant universal break.
question: How long must your data stay private?
lines: Why change encryption before a powerful enough quantum computer exists? Because some information must stay private for years.
An attacker could record encrypted traffic now and hope to decrypt it later with future capabilities.
Post quantum cryptography uses algorithms designed to resist known quantum attacks. It runs on ordinary computers.
This does not mean every kind of encryption is already broken, or that a quantum laptop is required.
Organizations are updating protocols and systems gradually. Long lived sensitive data is an important reason to prepare.
